title: Jan 2024
des: DOH (HAAD) paediatrics recall, January 2024 (notes scanned 17 Jan 2024)

questions.question: A child fell and has an open supracondylar fracture. The radial pulse cannot be felt but the hand is warm and viable. Which option is NOT appropriate?
questions.exp: An open fracture needs antibiotics, washout and urgent fixation; a pulseless (even pink) hand needs Doppler and early reduction, with exploration if the pulse does not return. Observation alone is wrong.

questions.question: A child has abdominal distension and gastroenteritis-like symptoms with mild bleeding. A picture is shown and Cryptosporidium is in the differential. Which organism is most likely?
questions.exp: The recall marked Cryptosporidium (the stem was only partly remembered: oocysts on modified Ziehl–Neelsen stain cause watery diarrhoea and bloating). Bloody diarrhoea is more typical of Entamoeba or Shigella, so treat this item as uncertain.

questions.question: A 2-year-old scribbles but does not know body parts and builds a tower of 6 cubes but not 8. What is his developmental level?
questions.exp: Milestones: tower of 6 cubes at 2 years (8 at 2½), scribbles at 15–18 months; points to body parts at 18–24 months. Not knowing body parts at 2 is a language/understanding delay. (Original options not recalled.)
questions.a: About 2 years in fine motor, but delayed in language/social understanding

questions.question: A 3-year-old with a viral URTI has a recurrent night-time cough. What is the treatment?
questions.exp: Post-viral cough is self-limiting; bronchodilators and inhaled steroids do not help without asthma features, and oral salbutamol is not recommended. The recall was uncertain.

questions.question: A local antibiotic guideline usually includes all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Antimicrobial stewardship guidelines give the drug, dose, route and shortest effective course, and favour narrow-spectrum agents.

questions.question: An 18-day-old neonate presents with poor feeding. Her mother had varicella 2 days before delivery. CSF shows raised protein, low glucose and lymphocytes; culture is negative. What is the treatment?
questions.exp: Neonatal meningoencephalitis with possible HSV/VZV: start IV aciclovir with antibiotics and await CSF PCR. VZIG is preventive and has no role once disease is established. The recall marked antibiotics for 14 days.
questions.d: IV antibiotics plus IV aciclovir while awaiting PCR

questions.question: An obese child has raised cholesterol and low HDL. What is the first advice?
questions.exp: Obesity-related dyslipidaemia is first treated with diet, physical activity and weight management. Statins are considered from 8–10 years only for persistent very high LDL (e.g. familial hypercholesterolaemia).
questions.d: Lifestyle advice: increase exercise and diet change

questions.question: Which statement about acute sinusitis in children is NOT true?
questions.exp: Most sinusitis is viral and settles in 10 days. Antibiotics (amoxicillin or co-amoxiclav) are for symptoms beyond 10 days, worsening ('double sickening') or severe disease.
questions.b: Symptoms under 10 days need analgesia only
questions.c: Symptoms lasting more than 10 days, or worsening, suggest bacterial sinusitis treated with co-amoxiclav

questions.question: A 14-year-old has irregular, heavy menstrual bleeding. Which step is NOT needed?
questions.exp: Work-up: pregnancy test, FBC and ferritin, TFT, coagulation (vWD screening) and ultrasound where needed. Repeating an FBC at every visit is unnecessary.
questions.c: Pregnancy test and pelvic ultrasound if indicated
questions.d: Full blood count at every visit

questions.question: Which is an indication for therapeutic hypothermia (cooling) in a newborn?
questions.exp: TOBY criteria (≥36 weeks): pH <7.0 or base deficit ≥16 within 60 minutes, or Apgar ≤5 at 10 minutes, or ongoing resuscitation at 10 minutes; plus moderate–severe encephalopathy. The recall marked pH <7.2.

questions.question: A 6-year-old has nocturnal enuresis that has not improved with behavioural measures. What is the next step?
questions.exp: NICE: the alarm is first-line after reward systems; desmopressin if the alarm fails or is unsuitable.

questions.question: An obese child (BMI over 35) is irritable in the morning, snores heavily and lacks concentration at school. What is the best investigation?
questions.exp: Obstructive sleep apnoea is confirmed by polysomnography (sleep study); overnight oximetry is a screening alternative.

questions.question: A child is inattentive, hyperactive and impulsive at home and at school for over 6 months. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: ADHD requires symptoms in two or more settings, starting before 12 years and lasting 6 months or more.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of short stature in boys?
questions.exp: Normal-variant short stature (familial and constitutional delay) far outnumbers endocrine causes.

questions.question: A boy is diagnosed with posterior urethral valves. Which is NOT done as an emergency?
questions.exp: Emergency management: bladder drainage (catheter), fluids and electrolytes, ultrasound and MCUG. DMSA is done later.

questions.question: Which statement about tonsillitis is NOT true?
questions.exp: Most sore throats are viral; use FeverPAIN/Centor to decide on penicillin V for 10 days. Avoid amoxicillin when glandular fever is possible because of the rash.
questions.a: Penicillin V is first-line for bacterial tonsillitis
questions.b: The decision about glandular fever can wait; there is no need to consider it
questions.c: Amoxicillin can cause a rash in EBV infection

questions.question: A child with fever and lymphadenopathy was given amoxicillin and then developed a rash. What is the most likely cause?
questions.exp: A maculopapular rash after amoxicillin is classic for EBV; it is not true penicillin allergy.

questions.question: Which condition is NOT inherited as autosomal dominant?
questions.exp: CF is autosomal recessive. (The recall listed junctional EB, acrodermatitis enteropathica and Menkes, which are recessive or X-linked too, so the options were rebuilt.)

questions.question: What is the first step in managing active Crohn's disease in a child?
questions.exp: Exclusive enteral nutrition for 6–8 weeks is first-line induction in paediatric luminal Crohn's: as effective as steroids, better for growth and mucosal healing.

questions.question: A child with sickle cell disease has pallor and abdominal pain that improved, with low Hb and high reticulocytes. Which crisis is it?
questions.exp: Sudden fall in Hb with high reticulocytes, abdominal pain and an enlarging spleen = splenic sequestration. Aplastic crisis (parvovirus) has low reticulocytes. The recall was unsure (vaso-occlusive vs aplastic).

questions.question: A 2-week-old breastfed baby is jaundiced, gaining weight and has no fever. What do you do?
questions.exp: Jaundice beyond 14 days needs a split bilirubin to exclude cholestasis (biliary atresia), plus stool colour; most will be breast milk jaundice.

questions.question: A child has transient synovitis after a viral illness but cannot bear weight on the joint. What do you do?
questions.exp: Typical transient synovitis in a well, afebrile child settles with rest and NSAIDs; return if fever or symptoms persist beyond a few days.
questions.c: Discharge with analgesia (NSAIDs) and safety-net advice

questions.question: Which test is used in Down syndrome antenatal screening?
questions.exp: First-trimester combined test: nuchal translucency, free β-hCG (high) and PAPP-A (low). Second-trimester quadruple test: AFP (low), oestriol (low), hCG (high), inhibin A (high). The recall was mixed.
